title: GAO Audit Finds All 24 CFO Act Federal Agencies Unprepared for Post-Quantum Cryptography Migration - Quantum Computing Report
gist: A GAO audit (GAO-27-108740) found none of the 24 CFO Act agencies have fully implemented OMB's core post-quantum cryptography preparation practices, with gaps in inventories, funding estimates and testing; OMB estimates $7.1 billion to migrate priority systems.

insights.claim: GAO's audit of all 24 CFO Act agencies found zero have fully implemented OMB's core practices for protecting unclassified federal IT systems against future quantum decryption.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Federal PQC readiness is far behind policy, which supports a long, funded PQC procurement cycle.
insights.locator: zero out of the 24 reviewed agencies

insights.claim: The public report is an unclassified release of a sensitive audit originally issued in September 2025, redacted by GAO with the Office of the National Cyber Director.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The findings are about a year old, so current agency status may be somewhat better than reported.
insights.locator: unclassified release of a sensitive audit

insights.claim: GAO measured agencies against three mandatory pillars: prioritized inventories of quantum-vulnerable cryptographic assets, multi-year migration funding assessments, and operational PQC algorithm testing.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: These three pillars are a checklist for sizing PQC vendor demand: discovery, budgeting, testing.

insights.claim: 23 of 24 agencies lack documented processes to maintain cryptographic inventories and 19 of 24 fail to use automated discovery tools.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Automated cryptographic discovery and CBOM tooling is an obvious near-term spend category.

insights.claim: Inventories omitted high-value assets, PKI systems and data sensitive past 2035, and some agencies misclassified symmetric algorithms as quantum-vulnerable.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Basic scoping errors suggest agencies need outside expertise, not just budget.

insights.claim: 21 of 24 agencies submitted incomplete migration cost projections and 3 submitted no funding data, partly because they lacked vendor price quotes for PQC-integrated commercial products.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Lack of vendor pricing leaves a gap that suppliers can fill with quotes to unlock agency budgets.

insights.claim: 23 of 24 agencies have executed no operational PQC software or hardware testing, and 18 of 24 report severe shortages of cryptography expertise and lack documented workforce training plans.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Talent scarcity is a binding constraint on migration pace regardless of funding.

insights.claim: The main urgency driver is 'harvest now, decrypt later': hostile states such as China may capture encrypted traffic today via BGP rerouting or subsea cable interception to decrypt once a cryptographically relevant quantum computer exists.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Data with long confidentiality lifetimes is already at risk, which justifies acting before CRQCs arrive.

insights.claim: Survey data cited by GAO indicates a majority of quantum experts predict a CRQC could arrive as soon as the 2030s.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The expert-survey timeline anchors the 2030 and 2035 migration deadlines.

insights.claim: OMB's government-wide rough-order estimate to migrate priority systems and replace non-upgradeable legacy infrastructure is $7.1 billion.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A $7.1B federal figure sets a floor for the addressable PQC migration market in government.

insights.claim: CNSSP 15 mandates PQC support for all new commercial National Security Systems starting in 2027 and a complete phase-out of legacy non-compliant hardware by 2030.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hard 2027 and 2030 dates create procurement deadlines for vendors.

insights.claim: In the underlying sensitive report GAO issued 89 targeted recommendations across 23 agencies, including enforcing automated CBOM inventories and establishing dedicated migration budgets.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Recommendations point to automated Cryptographic Bill of Materials tooling and dedicated budget lines.
